info.name: Domestic Connects - Worker Lifecycle (Integration)
info.description:
End-to-end integration suite for the Domestic Connects microservice platform. Exercises the full worker lifecycle through the API gateway (http://localhost:8080/api/**):

  0. Register worker/employer/admin accounts and log all three in
  1. Employer posts a job and assigns the worker
  2. Attendance is marked for several days of the month
  3. Salary slip PDF is generated, downloaded, history + CSV + batch ZIP verified
  4. Performance review is submitted and read back
  5. Notifications are received for each triggering event (job-assigned, salary-slip-generated, performance-reviewed)
  6. Admin dashboard analytics reflect all of the above

One infrastructure gap of the current platform is covered by a companion script in integration-tests/scripts (see integration-tests/README.md): no service publishes Kafka notification events yet, so scripts/publish-notification-events.sh simulates the producers.

Run headlessly with scripts/run-newman.sh or interactively in Postman by following the manual walkthrough in integration-tests/README.md.

exec: // Seed run-scoped data ONCE: unique emails, passwords and the current month/year.
// In phased Newman runs the wrapper pre-supplies these via --environment, so
// the seed is skipped when workerEmail already exists anywhere.

item.name: 0. Register Accounts
item.description: Creates the three accounts used across the whole lifecycle: a WORKER, an EMPLOYER and an ADMIN. Registration returns JWT access tokens and immediately usable (active) accounts — there is no email verification step.

item.name: NEGATIVE: duplicate worker registration is rejected

exec: pm.test('Conflict message mentions the existing email',()=>pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include('already exists'));

item.name: 1. Login & Activate
item.description: Logs all three users in, exercises the deactivate -> login-rejected -> reactivate -> login-ok cycle, and refreshes the worker's access token.

item.name: NEGATIVE: login while deactivated is rejected
2. Job Posting & Assignment
item.description: The EMPLOYER posts a job with a daily wage, verifies it is listed, then assigns the WORKER to it. A WORKER may apply (self-assign), but negative cases prove WORKERs cannot create jobs or assign other workers.

exec: pm.test('Job starts OPEN with the requested wage',()=>{pm.expect(json.status).to.eql('OPEN');pm.expect(Number(json.wagePerDay)).to.eql(500);});

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Household Helper - {{month}}/{{year}}",
  "description": "Daily cleaning, cooking and errand support for a family of four. Reliable and punctual worker required for the full month.",
  "employerId": "{{employerId}}",
  "wagePerDay": 500.0,
  "location": "Bengaluru, Karnataka"
}

exec: pm.test('Listing is an array containing the new job',()=>{pm.expect(json).to.be.an('array');const j=json.find(x=>String(x.id)===pm.collectionVariables.get('jobId'));pm.expect(j).to.be.an('object');pm.expect(j.status).to.eql('OPEN');});

pm.test('Listing is an array of WORKERs containing the bootstrapped worker',()=>{pm.expect(json.data).to.be.an('array');const w=json.data.find(u=>String(u.id)===pm.variables.get('workerId'));pm.expect(w).to.be.an('object');pm.expect(w.role).to.eql('WORKER');});

item.name: Employer assigns worker to the job
NEGATIVE: worker cannot assign another worker

exec: pm.test('Worker assigning a different user is rejected (403)',()=>pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.eql(403));
pm.test('Message mentions workers may only apply for themselves',()=>pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include('only apply'));

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Gardener & Cleaner - {{month}}/{{year}}",
  "description": "Weekly gardening and outdoor cleaning for a private home.",
  "employerId": "{{employerId}}",
  "wagePerDay": 400.0,
  "location": "Mysuru, Karnataka"
}

item.name: Worker applies (self-assigns) to the second job
NEGATIVE: worker cannot create a job post

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Should not be allowed",
  "description": "This request must be rejected with 403 because WORKERs cannot post jobs.",
  "employerId": "{{employerId}}",
  "wagePerDay": 100.0,
  "location": "Nowhere"
}

item.name: 3. Attendance
item.description: The EMPLOYER marks attendance for the worker over several days of the current month (3 PRESENT, 1 HALF_DAY, 1 ABSENT) and verifies the monthly report and summary. Duplicate marking is rejected with 409. The WORKER can read their own monthly report (self-service); reading another user's report is rejected with 403.

item.name: NEGATIVE: duplicate attendance for day 1 is rejected
Worker attendance report for the month
NEGATIVE: worker cannot view another worker's attendance
4. Salary Slip & Payroll
item.description: Generates and downloads the monthly salary slip PDF for the worker, verifies the persisted history (3 present days + 0.5 half-day at 500/day = 1750.00), exports history as CSV and downloads the batch ZIP of slips. A worker with no attendance returns 404.

item.name: Salary history reflects the generated record

exec: pm.test('CSV body contains the header and the gross salary',()=>{const body=pm.response.text();pm.expect(body).to.include('Gross Salary');pm.expect(body).to.include('1750.00');});

item.name: NEGATIVE: slip for a user with no attendance returns 404
5. Performance Review
item.description: The EMPLOYER submits a performance review for the assigned worker (rating 4), verifies the aggregated report, confirms the WORKER can read their own reviews, rejects cross-worker reads, and updates the review to rating 5.

body.raw:
{
  "workerId": "{{workerId}}",
  "jobId": "{{jobId}}",
  "rating": 4,
  "remarks": "Consistent, punctual and very reliable. Great with the children.",
  "reviewedBy": "{{employerName}}"
}

item.name: NEGATIVE: worker cannot read another worker's performance
Employer updates the review to rating 5
6. Notifications
item.description: Verifies the worker receives one notification per triggering event (JOB_ASSIGNED, SALARY_SLIP_GENERATED, PERFORMANCE_REVIEWED). No service publishes these events yet, so run scripts/publish-notification-events.sh first (the run-newman.sh wrapper does this automatically).

item.name: Worker inbox contains a notification for every event type

exec: pm.test('Inbox is an array with at least 3 notifications',()=>pm.expect(json.length).to.be.at.least(3));

item.name: Worker marks a notification as read
NEGATIVE: employer cannot read the worker's inbox
7. Admin Dashboard
item.description: The ADMIN verifies the dashboard summary and analytics reflect everything done above: 3+ users, the assigned job, a non-zero monthly attendance rate and a non-zero average performance rating. Non-ADMIN roles are blocked.

item.name: Dashboard summary reflects the lifecycle data

exec: pm.test('Monthly attendance rate is present and > 0',()=>{pm.expect(d.monthlyAttendanceRate).to.not.eql(null);pm.expect(d.monthlyAttendanceRate).to.be.above(0);});
pm.test('Average performance rating is present and > 0',()=>{pm.expect(d.averagePerformanceRating).to.not.eql(null);pm.expect(d.averagePerformanceRating).to.be.above(0);});

item.name: Dashboard analytics reflect all lifecycle steps

exec: pm.test('usersByRole counts at least 1 WORKER and 1 EMPLOYER',()=>{pm.expect(d.usersByRole.WORKER).to.be.at.least(1);pm.expect(d.usersByRole.EMPLOYER).to.be.at.least(1);});

item.name: Admin user listing contains the worker
NEGATIVE: employer cannot access admin analytics
